title: Missing From<mail_parser::DateTime> for HeaderDateTime (and reverse) — uses free fns instead of From trait
description: header_typed.rs:97 and 111 define private `fn to_mail_parser(self) -> mail_parser::DateTime` and `fn from_mail_parser(dt: &mail_parser::DateTime) -> Self`. These are natural `From` conversions: `impl From<mail_parser::DateTime> for HeaderDateTime` and `impl From<HeaderDateTime> for mail_parser::DateTime`. Using `From` instead would (a) follow the standard Rust naming convention reviewers expect, (b) enable `.into()` at call sites including `MessageStream::new(buf).parse_date().into()`-style chains, (c) give callers an obvious extension point if they ever need the conversion (currently impossible — fns are private). The free-fn names also do not match Rust convention: `Self::from_mail_parser` would be more idiomatic than a bare `from_mail_parser` if a `From` impl really is undesirable, but the right answer is `From`.
close_reason: Won't fix: implementing From<mail_parser::DateTime> for HeaderDateTime (and the reverse) would expose mail_parser::DateTime in mime-tree's public API. mime-tree/AGENTS.md explicitly forbids this: 'No mail-parser types in public API.' The conversion helpers stay private. MIME-o2c.33 (asymmetric borrow on the same helpers) is closed by the same batch.
